primary_decoupling.activity_to_decouple: Integrate the workspace with external apps and continuously iterate/update the system over time
primary_decoupling.from_incumbent_bundle: Today this activity is bundled across (1) Notion’s core all-in-one workspace product and its native integration touchpoints and (2) the customer’s own manual, ongoing maintenance work across connected external tools (e.g., Slack/Google Drive) (E6,E12,E13).
primary_decoupling.customer_pain: Integrations and ongoing iteration are a recurring “eroding” stage: users must constantly connect tools, troubleshoot broken connections/permissions, and refactor their workspace as it evolves—creating continuous time/effort tax and brittleness (E12,E13).
primary_decoupling.new_offering: Notion Integration & Maintenance Copilot: an AI-assisted “integration doctor” that (a) sets up/updates integrations from plain-English intent, (b) proactively detects and guides fixes for broken links/permissions/sync issues, and (c) recommends safe, incremental workspace refactors—without requiring users to move their artifacts out of Notion (E6,E12,E13,E15). (Framed as a decoupling wedge per Teixeira’s decoupling logic; primary source: books/unlocking-the-customer-value-chain-chapter-1.md.)
primary_decoupling.why_customer_switches: Users can keep their existing tools and workflows but offload the most painful, repetitive maintenance work to Notion—getting a workspace that “stays working” with less manual setup and firefighting, while still using the same external apps (E12,E13).

do_not_decouple.activity: Create and store work artifacts (notes, databases, wikis, project boards)
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t unbundle the core artifact-creation/storage layer: it is the primary locus of customer value creation in an all-in-one workspace and the foundation for owning the user relationship and repeat behavior; decoupling here would weaken the core usage engine (E6,E9).

do_not_decouple.activity: Collaborate by sharing, commenting, and coordinating tasks on shared pages
do_not_decouple.reason: Avoid decoupling collaboration because it is tightly coupled to the shared-page artifact layer and team coordination inside the workspace; unbundling it would dilute the product’s integrated value proposition and risk pushing teams to keep collaboration elsewhere (E6,E11).

do_not_decouple.activity: Discover and consider a workspace tool through word-of-mouth, online content, and/or by encountering it via other tools
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t attack discovery as the wedge: it’s largely a channel/awareness activity rather than a workflow “job step” Notion can uniquely own, and it doesn’t directly reduce the recurring integration/maintenance pain that drives ongoing retention (E7,E12,E13).

do_not_decouple.activity: Sign up and complete initial onboarding to access the workspace
do_not_decouple.reason: Avoid making onboarding the primary decoupling target because it is relatively infrequent (one-time per user) versus the recurring erosion in integration + iteration; focusing here risks optimizing a smaller pain point while missing the highest-leverage weak link (E8,E12,E13).
